purpose: Tracked, self-contained inputs for the P3-C PR-4A cost/token provenance gate (tests/unit/eval/pr4a-cost-provenance-gate.test.ts). The bytes are the FROZEN PR-4A eval artifacts: they are copied verbatim from the gitignored work/ drop so the gate can judge the historical artifact in a clean checkout, where work/ does not exist.

frozenFrom.whyCopy: work/ is gitignored (.gitignore:8), so a clean checkout has no such inputs
frozenFrom.method: Copy-Item of each file into tests/fixtures/pr4a/, then byte-for-byte compare (SHA256 over the raw file bytes) and an LF/NUL/BOM check; the digests below are the MEASURED values of both the source and the copy on that timestamp

eolPolicy.rule: every fixture file is plain LF text
eolPolicy.enforcement: tests/fixtures/pr4a/.gitattributes pins text eol=lf for this directory so a core.autocrlf=true checkout cannot rewrite the frozen bytes; the test re-checks bytes + sha256 + absence of CR/NUL/BOM at run time
eolPolicy.measured: this workstation has core.autocrlf=true. Measured on 2026-10-30: an UNDECLARED .jsonl checked out through git becomes CRLF (sha256 would change and all five cases would go red), while a .jsonl declared text eol=lf in this directory keeps its LF bytes. The policy is therefore load-bearing, not decorative.
eolPolicy.policyFileIsNotData: .gitattributes is NOT listed in files[]: it is policy, not a fixture. Removing it does not change the five P3-C cases (they verify bytes+sha256 on the files they read), so the deletion experiment shows it as "optional" — but the meta-test tests/unit/meta/no-work-dependency.test.ts catches the removal directly: with the file parked, `git check-attr` reports text/eol "unspecified" and that case fails (exit 1) naming "every frozen fixture must be declared text eol=lf"; restoring the file returns the byte-identical sha256.

deletionExperiment.rule: A-t8-2 minimality: copy the fixture set to a temp dir, delete ONE file, point PR4A_FIXTURE_DIR at the copy and re-run tests/unit/eval/pr4a-cost-provenance-gate.test.ts
deletionExperiment.command: node work/t8-probe/minimality.mjs (throwaway probe; the same experiment is re-runnable by deleting any single file from a copy of this directory)

perFile.removed: exit=1 (no tests collected: the manifest load throws)
perFile.verdict: required (deleting it turns all five cases RED)
optional: deleting it leaves the five P3-C cases GREEN, so it is NOT their input; it is kept because it is the reproducible input for the verifier ledger assertions named in servesAssertions

deletionExperiment.twoLayerRule: `optional` is NOT "may be missing from a checkout". Measured with node work/t8-probe/optional-two-layers.mjs (2026-10-30T05:15): with pr4a-ledger-Arm-2.jsonl parked, the 5 P3-C cases stay GREEN (exit 0) while tests/unit/meta/no-work-dependency.test.ts goes RED naming "pr4a-ledger-Arm-2.jsonl must be present in the checkout"; restoring the file returns the byte-identical sha256.

servesAssertions: justification: the ONLY input the five P3-C cases mutate and judge; without it the verifier cannot parse the report at all (json-parses fails)
